title: The Eyes Are The (Context) Window to The Soul: How Windsurf Gets to Know You — Sam Fertig, Windsurf
talk_summary: A Windsurf forward-deployed engineer argues that coding-agent quality comes from curating relevant context (user state + codebase state) rather than maximizing context-window size, and frames latency as a core feature. The talk is mostly conceptual/marketing with no measured results, but the 'what context and how much' framing and the heuristic-vs-hard-evidence split are copyable.

takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly optimize for which context enters the window instead of growing the window, and treat latency as a first-class feature of the agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have found much better results by optimizing for what context gets put into that window instead of just trying to make it bigger

takeaways.technique: Two-bucket context model (user state vs codebase state)
takeaways.what_they_do: They split context into heuristics about the user's behavior (recent files, clipboard, terminal, what they're trying to do) and hard evidence (code, docs, rules, memories), then combine both with the prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's your prompt plus the state of your codebase plus the user state.

takeaways.technique: Agent-generated memories and rules as durable context
takeaways.what_they_do: They list 'memories that the agent generates about you' and 'rules that you provide' as first-class hard-evidence context sources alongside code and docs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: memories that the agent generates about you, right? More code, lots and lots of code

takeaways.what_they_do: They expose many retrieval mechanisms (embedding search, plain-text search, reranking, parsing, remote indexing) and pick among them rather than relying on one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: embedding search, memories, rules, custom workspaces, app mentions, plain text search, knowledge base, multimodal input, rip tide, MCP, remote indexing, reranking

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat latency not as a preference but as a core feature of a good coding agent, which motivates context curation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that also helps solve the issue of latency which is not just a preference thing but a a core feature of good AI coding agents
